guard: the describe bootstrap carries the reserved reply-to so an absent endpoint produces broker-attested no-responders instead of consuming the full reply deadline
why: Every generic manager invocation starts with describe. epCall already used the reserved
no-responders sentinel, but describe did not request broker feedback at all, so a missing
manager and a subscribed-but-silent handler both became the same full-budget timeout.
This mutation restores that exact omission. The smoke uses a real NATS broker and an actually
absent endpoint; the named cell requires the broker's immediate unavailable verdict and its
no-responders observation rather than a hand-built error.

mutations.name: describe publishes without the reserved no-responders reply-to
mutations.expectRed: describe with no subscriber gets the broker's immediate `unavailable`, not a reply deadline
mutations.cell: describe with no subscriber gets the broker's immediate `unavailable`, not a reply deadline
